title: Evaluation plan charter
summary: This intermediate-level resource explains why the requested citation correction is blocked and what a practitioner must obtain before making a correction-only change. It prevents an unsupported source replacement from altering material whose reviewed baseline is unavailable.
prerequisites: The current evaluation plan charter JSON file
The provenance record for the citation being corrected
The claims or procedures supported by that citation

sections.title: Answer and change status
paragraphs: Practitioner question: Can I safely correct the evaluation plan charter from the supplied information? No. The current resource, its reviewed wording, and its prior citation metadata were not supplied. Obtain that baseline before editing. If it cannot be obtained, stop the correction and ask the resource owner to recover the last reviewed revision.

Which cited source changed and what did the change affect? UNKNOWN. The supplied citation inventory identifies only content/resources/evaluation-safety/evaluation-plan-charter.json as an unregistered publisher value that has never been verified. It provides no former source URL, replacement URL, title, publisher, movement record, or source-to-claim mapping. If those records remain unavailable, do not assert that a particular source moved or that particular statements were affected.

Because the affected material is UNKNOWN, no substantive correction can be distinguished from a rewrite. Material unaffected by the change also cannot be identified. The safe next action is to recover the existing file and source history rather than reconstructing the guide from assumptions.

sections.title: Correction procedure
paragraphs: Step 1: Recover the current JSON file at the revision intended for correction. Compare it with the prior reviewed revision so unchanged fields and prose can be preserved. If either revision is unavailable, stop and request it from the repository or editorial owner rather than recreating missing content.

Step 2: Establish the citation's provenance by recording its former HTTPS URL, current HTTPS URL, title, publisher, previous verification date, and the evidence that it moved or passed its review cadence. If the URL or publisher cannot be established, record the source identity as UNKNOWN and do not substitute a merely similar source.

Step 3: Map the changed source to every sentence, procedure, and expected-evidence statement that relies on it. If the mapping cannot be demonstrated from the existing resource or its review record, ask the prior reviewer or subject-matter owner to establish the mapping before editing.

Step 4: Review the replacement source and determine whether its relevant content changed. The National Institute of Standards and Technology describes documenting context, intended purposes, methods, measurements, responsibilities, prioritized risks, and responses as parts of AI risk management, but it does not define the exact structure of this platform's evaluation plan charter. If the replacement source does not support an existing claim, revise or remove only that claim and send the discrepancy for subject-matter review.

Step 5: Apply the smallest possible patch to the affected citation metadata and dependent text. Compare the result with the recovered baseline. If unrelated metadata, prose, procedures, or section identifiers changed, revert those changes and repeat the comparison.

Step 6: Validate the corrected object against the platform requirements and test every cited HTTPS URL. If parsing, schema validation, catalogue checks, or URL resolution fails, correct the failing value or restore the baseline and leave the update uncommitted.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence consists of the recovered baseline resource, the prior reviewed revision, the former and replacement source metadata, a record explaining why review was triggered, a source-to-claim mapping, the minimal patch, and successful parsing, schema, catalogue, and HTTPS-resolution results.

Verify success by comparing the patch with the baseline and confirming that only the changed citation and the material demonstrably affected by it differ. Independently open every final source URL over HTTPS, confirm its title and publisher, and record a non-future verification date.

The correction is not verified while the changed source, its affected claims, or the unchanged baseline remains UNKNOWN. If any of those conditions persists, keep the update blocked and return it to the editorial owner with the missing evidence identified.
